title: "Over-the-Air (OTA) Update"
description: "A remote delivery and installation of software or model changes on a connected device without requiring a physical service connection."
term: "Over-the-Air (OTA) Update"
letter: "O"
category: "Robotics"
difficulty: "Advanced"
---

## Simple explanation

An over-the-air (OTA) update lets a connected device receive new software
remotely. In robotics and edge AI, an update may include application code,
firmware, configuration, or model files.

## Technical explanation

An OTA update system distributes artifacts to devices over a network,
verifies their authenticity and integrity, installs them, and reports
status. Reliable designs consider staged rollout, compatibility,
interrupted downloads, rollback, access control, and recovery when an
update fails.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Devices deployed in the field may need model or software improvements
without physical access. Poor update design can leave devices unusable or
running incompatible components, so secure delivery and a tested recovery
path are core reliability requirements.

## How it works

A management service selects eligible devices and publishes a signed
update manifest or artifact. A device verifies the update, checks storage
and compatibility, installs it, and reports health. Rollouts can begin
with a small cohort and expand only after checks pass.

## Practical example

A fleet of inspection robots could receive an updated vision model in
stages. Each robot verifies the downloaded artifact, switches to the new
version only after validation, and retains a known-good version for
recovery if health checks fail.

## Common misconceptions

- An OTA update is not simply a file download; authenticity, installation, and recovery matter.
- A valid signature verifies the publisher and integrity, not that the update is correct or safe for every device.
- Updating model weights can change behavior even when application software stays unchanged.
